A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LaSRO work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–F are readable and support comparison; the additional page in v2 partly reflects layout spillover.

before.justification: v1 reports original reward-fine-tuning experiments, baseline comparisons and ablations in Table 1 and Figures 4–5, with further empirical analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and additionally reports computational timings and qualitative observations about reward-noise robustness.

M1.justification: The surrogate architecture, two-stage training procedure, online adaptation and losses remain unchanged. Naming the existing loss as Bradley–Terry-based and clarifying sampling do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Section 6.3 newly reports testing with manually perturbed ground-truth rewards, adding a briefly described noisy-feedback condition. T2I-prompt-873K, MJHQ-30K, T2I-CompBench and the three image-generation tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain RLCM/DDPO, PSO/Diff-DPO, GORS-LCM and the same distilled-model baselines. The direct-reward-gradient and other ablation variants also already appeared in v1; additional citations do not introduce evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The newly mentioned robustness check manually perturbs the target reward, although its noise distribution and magnitude are unspecified. Existing splits, metrics, checkpoint selection and training schedules remain unchanged; the added hardware and timing information documents existing experiments.

E4.justification: Section 6.3 adds a qualitative reward-noise robustness finding, and Appendix D states that sampling strategy is not critical provided initial noise varies. No supporting curves or detailed sensitivity results are added; the existing ablations and appendix analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. Appendix A retains the same estimation over 1,000 sampled prompt/noise pairs, with no changed statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the benchmark curves are unchanged, including the two-step LaSRO Image Reward of 0.998. Appendix D newly reports approximately 0.15-second inference and 12-hour/48-hour pre-training/fine-tuning times. Qualitative reward-noise and sampling-sensitivity findings are also added.

T1.justification: The formal definitions, losses, Lipschitz construction and value-based-RL derivation in Appendices A–C are retained. Section 5.3 changes explanatory prose, while Figure 2 corrects time-argument labels to match the existing mathematical definition.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution bullets retain the same claims about arbitrary-reward fine-tuning, ultra-few-step generation, superiority over policy-based baselines and the connection to value-based RL. The shortened conclusion does not materially change their scope.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 revises the mechanism explanation around gradient-noise reduction and off-policy exploration. Section 6.3 newly invokes reward-noise robustness to explain the advantage over direct reward gradients, while Appendix D qualifies sampling flexibility by requiring varying initial noise.

D1.justification: Appendix D adds inference timing for a 1024-by-1024 image on an A100 and training times on eight H100 GPUs, and explicitly describes random prompt/noise sampling. Existing hyperparameters and code/data access links are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Bradley–Terry, FIND, Step-aware Preference Optimization and a diffusion-RL tutorial/review. It removes the Soft Actor-Critic reference and revises the value-based-RL positioning in Section 5.3, without substantially expanding the literature discussion.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites affect Sections 5–6 and Appendices D–E, alongside terminology corrections and the affiliation change from Zoom Video Communications to Zoom Communications. The overall section order and narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 corrects its time-input labels; the remaining plots, examples and table structures are retained. Appendix text reflows, separating the Appendix F heading from Figure 9 and leaving PDF page 18 mostly empty.

improvement.justification: Appendix D's concrete hardware and timing disclosures improve transparency about computational cost, while the loss attribution and localized explanations improve clarity. These gains are limited: the main empirical evidence and formal analysis are unchanged, and the new reward-noise robustness assertion lacks a detailed protocol or quantitative support.
